transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, well, what finally scared me into coming in is that I keep making these really, really dumb technical mistakes at work. Stuff I absolutely know better than to make. I do camera work and editing, mostly freelance, and recently I was on this documentary shoot—which was wild, by the way, we were out in the woods for three days and it rained the entire time. My favorite boots are actually still completely ruined. I bought them at REI like five years ago and they were supposed to be totally waterproof, but I guess that wears off? I should probably spray them with that silicone stuff. My brother swears by it for his camping gear, he goes up to Yosemite every single summer and always tries to drag me along, but I hate sleeping in tents... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Right, work. The mistakes. Yeah, so I'll do things like label the camera cards wrong, or I'll just completely miss a timecode note from the director. It's so frustrating because I'll literally export a client cut with the completely wrong lower-third graphic on the screen, even after I've specifically checked it! Like, I will sit there, watch the timeline, and still send it out wrong. It's just getting to the point where I'm afraid I'm going to lose clients over it.
How are you feeling about making these mistakes at work?

It feels awful. Like, really embarrassing, because I know my actual camera work is top-notch. I just shot this beautiful sequence last week using a vintage anamorphic lens I found on eBay—which, by the way, I had to bid on at like 3 AM because the seller was in Germany and the time difference is brutal. I love finding weird old lenses, they give digital footage so much character. The newer glass is just too clinical, you know? My friend Sarah shoots on these high-end Arri Primes and they literally cost more than my car, but I honestly prefer the cheap vintage stuff... 

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. You asked how I feel about the mistakes. Right. 

Um, it sucks. Because of those dumb errors, my producers have definitely started trusting me less on the really complex shoots. And that's exactly the stuff I want to be doing. I've been working so hard to move into a senior director of photography role, and I can just feel that chance slipping away from me right now, completely despite the fact that the quality of my actual shooting is great. It's just so frustrating.
Do you find yourself forgetting things that you would normally remember?

No, not really? My memory is actually pretty solid. I don't really forget appointments or, like, where I put my keys or anything like that. I actually have this weirdly good memory for really random details, like I can remember the exact coffee order of a director I worked with five years ago. He always wanted a half-caf oat milk latte with exactly two pumps of sugar-free vanilla, which is just such a specific order. 

Oat milk is literally everywhere now, though. I actually tried making my own oat milk at home once because I bought this ridiculously fancy blender. It's a Vitamix. Honestly, best purchase of my life. You can make hot soup in it just from the friction of the blades! I made this roasted red pepper soup last week, but I accidentally dropped a whole extra clove of raw garlic in and it was intensely spicy. Garlic is weird like that, right? Like, if you roast it, it gets super sweet and mellow, almost like butter, but raw it just burns your whole mouth... 

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, memory. Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem with forgetting things. It's just the in-the-moment dumb mistakes that are killing me.
Do you feel anxious or sad most of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or sad. I mean, I get stressed out about work sometimes, obviously, especially when I mess up, but I'm generally a pretty upbeat person. I actually have a ton of energy most days. I try to burn it off by going for runs, usually in the mornings. 

I live right near this really nice trail system that goes all the way around the lake. It's beautiful, especially in the fall when the leaves change. I was out there yesterday and I saw this massive blue heron just standing perfectly still in the shallows. They look almost prehistoric, you know? Like pterodactyls or something. I actually tried to get a video of it on my phone, but phone cameras are just terrible for wildlife. The digital zoom completely ruins the image quality. Apple keeps saying their cameras are getting better, but unless you have actual optical zoom, it's just cropping the sensor and making it pixelated. I really should just start carrying a small mirrorless camera with a decent telephoto lens when I run, but then it bounces around too much...

Wait, sorry. No, I don't feel sad or anxious. Just frustrated with myself sometimes.
Do you find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time?

Well, I guess I'm not really sure if I find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time. I mean, when I'm shooting, I'm totally dialed in. But maybe with other stuff? Like, I tried reading this book recently—it was a biography of Stanley Kubrick, which is fascinating because his process was just insane. Did you know he made Shelley Duvall do 127 takes of the baseball bat scene in *The Shining*? That's just cruel, honestly. I get wanting the perfect shot, but there's a point where you're just torturing your actors. 

I actually worked with a director once who thought he was Kubrick. He would make us reset these massive lighting rigs for, like, a half-inch difference in a shadow. It drove the gaffer absolutely crazy. Gaffers are the unsung heroes of film sets, by the way. They know more about electricity than most engineers. My buddy Dave is a gaffer and he built this custom LED panel from scratch using parts he bought at a hardware store... 

Anyway, I don't know. I guess I haven't really noticed if I have trouble focusing for a long time. It probably just depends on what I'm doing.
Do you often find yourself getting distracted when you're in the middle of a task?

Distracted? Um, I don't think so? I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed if I do. Like, when I'm editing, I'm just in the zone. I actually just upgraded my editing suite at home. I got one of those curved ultrawide monitors, and let me tell you, it completely changes the workflow. You can have your entire timeline stretched out without having to constantly zoom in and out. 

Although, the color grading on it was a little tricky to calibrate at first. I had to buy this special little sensor thing that you hang over the screen. It reads the ambient light in the room, which is super important because if your room is too warm, your color grade will end up looking way too cool when someone watches it on their TV. My living room has these huge south-facing windows, which is great for my plants—I have this massive Monstera that's practically taking over a corner—but it's a nightmare for screen glare. I ended up having to install these heavy blackout curtains. They're velvet, which I thought would look really dramatic and cool, but they actually just attract so much dust. I feel like I'm constantly having to vacuum them. 

But yeah, I don't really know if I get distracted in the middle of things. I just kind of do what needs to get done, you know?
Do you find it difficult to complete tasks because your mind starts to wander?

Tasks? I mean, I don't really know if my mind wanders that much. I guess I just kind of bounce around until things are finished. Like yesterday, I was supposed to be organizing all my old hard drives. I have literally dozens of them just stacked in my office because I never delete raw footage. You never know when you might need a B-roll shot of, like, a generic cityscape or a pigeon walking on a sidewalk. 

Anyway, I was pulling them all out, and I found this one drive from a documentary I worked on like five years ago. We were following this guy who built miniature medieval castles out of Popsicle sticks. It was the weirdest project, but he was so passionate about it. He actually had a whole working drawbridge on one of them. It made me realize I haven't done anything hands-on like that in ages. I used to build model airplanes when I was a kid. The glue smelled terrible, but there was something so satisfying about putting the decals on perfectly. I wonder if they still make those kits? I should probably check Amazon. Honestly, you can find anything on there now, it's kind of terrifying how much they have. 

But um, what were we talking about? Completing tasks? I don't know, I usually get them done eventually, so I haven't really thought about it.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I usually have a reason for the things I do, so I wouldn't say I don't think them through. Like, I guess some people might say buying my new drone last week was impulsive, but I actually really needed it for this indie feature I'm shooting next month. Have you seen the footage these new DJI drones can get? It's unbelievable. It's basically a flying cinema camera. 

Though, the regulations now are a total nightmare. You have to get your Part 107 license if you want to fly commercially, which makes sense, but the test is surprisingly hard. It's all this aeronautical chart reading and weather patterns. My buddy Greg took it three times before he passed. He's the one who actually got me into drones. He crashed his first one straight into Lake Tahoe. Just... right into the water. We actually had to rent a boat to go try and find it, which was a complete disaster. He was talking about hiring a scuba diver to get it back, which is crazy because the memory card was probably fried anyway. I really want to get scuba certified, though. I saw this documentary about the Great Barrier Reef last year and the coral bleaching is just heartbreaking. It makes you want to go see it before it's completely gone, you know? 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about thinking things through? Yeah, I don't know, I guess I just do what makes sense at the time, so I wouldn't really call it acting on impulse.
Do you often find that you're unable to concentrate on a single task for as long as you need to?

Concentrate on a single task? Hmm, I don't really know if I have a problem with that. I mean, I feel like I concentrate fine when I need to. Like, when I'm syncing audio to video, you really have to pay attention to the waveforms. It's super tedious, but I can sit there and do it. 

Actually, speaking of audio, I just bought this vintage microphone at a flea market over the weekend. It's an old ribbon mic from, like, the 1950s. The guy selling it had no idea what he had. He thought it was just some old radio prop. I couldn't believe it. I'm going to have to get it refurbished, though, because the ribbon inside is super fragile. You can literally blow it out just by breathing on it too hard. There's this guy in Chicago who specializes in fixing them, but his waitlist is like six months long. Chicago is such a great city, though. I went there for a film festival a few years ago and had the best deep-dish pizza of my life. I know people say it's just a casserole, but honestly, if it tastes that good, who cares what you call it? I've been trying to perfect my own pizza dough at home, but I can never get the hydration right. The flour makes a huge difference. You really need that 00 flour they use in Italy. I found this specialty Italian grocer across town that sells it, but the traffic to get there is always a nightmare. 

Sorry, what was the question? Something about concentrating? Yeah, I don't know, I guess I haven't really noticed if I can't concentrate. I usually just power through whatever I'm doing.
Do you have trouble controlling your emotions when you're under stress?

Trouble controlling my emotions? I mean, stress is just part of the job, right? I don't think I lose control or anything. Like, when we're on set and the lighting isn't right, or we're losing daylight, you just have to figure it out. 

Although, losing daylight is the worst. We were shooting this outdoor commercial for a local car dealership last month, and the sun was going down so fast. The director was getting super anxious, and the actor—this guy who usually does theater—kept forgetting his lines. Theater actors are so different from screen actors. They always project way too much, like they're trying to reach the back row of an auditorium, even when the boom mic is literally two feet above their head. I actually did some theater in college. I was the stage manager for a production of *A Midsummer Night's Dream*. It was so much fun, but the guy playing Puck accidentally knocked over a whole rack of costumes backstage during opening night. It was a disaster. I had to sew a tear in Titania's dress with like, three minutes before her cue. I'm actually pretty good at sewing. My grandmother taught me when I was little. She used to make all her own clothes back in the sixties. She had this beautiful vintage Singer sewing machine that weighed a ton. I think my aunt has it now. I should ask her about it. I've been wanting to try making my own curtains for the living room because the ones you buy at the store are always the wrong length, or the fabric feels super cheap, you know? 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about stress? Yeah, I don't know, I just deal with it like anyone else, I guess. I wouldn't say I have trouble controlling my emotions.
Do you ever feel overwhelmed by your emotions?

Overwhelmed? Um, no, not really. I mean, I have emotions like anyone else, but I wouldn't say they overwhelm me. I usually just keep moving, you know? Like, there's always something else to focus on. 

Especially when I'm editing. You get so deep into the timeline that you kind of forget about everything else. I was editing this wedding video last week—which I usually hate doing, honestly, weddings are just so stressful and the brides always want everything to look like a movie, but they only hire one shooter. Anyway, the couple had this gorgeous outdoor ceremony at this botanical garden. The flowers were incredible. There were these massive hydrangeas everywhere. I actually tried planting hydrangeas in my front yard last spring, but I think the soil is too alkaline or something because they never bloomed. I read somewhere that you can change the color of hydrangea blooms by adding coffee grounds to the soil, which is wild. I drink so much coffee, I should definitely try that. I have this espresso machine that I absolutely love. It took me forever to learn how to dial in the grind size, though. If it's too fine, it chokes the machine, and if it's too coarse, it just tastes like sour water. There's this local roaster downtown that gets these amazing single-origin beans from Ethiopia. The flavor notes are literally like blueberry and jasmine. It's so good. I usually buy two bags at a time so I don't run out. 

Sorry, what was the question? Overwhelmed by emotions? Yeah, no, I think I handle things fine. I just stay busy, I guess.
Do you often find your mind jumping from one thought to another when you're trying to focus?

My mind jumping? Hmm, I don't know if I'd say that. When I'm trying to focus, I just do the thing, you know? Like, if I'm setting up a shot, I'm just looking at the framing and the lighting. 

Speaking of lighting, I really need to replace the bulbs in my kitchen. They're those awful fluorescent tubes that make everything look green. It's impossible to tell if food is cooked right under that light. I was trying to make a risotto the other night, and I swear the mushrooms looked gray. Risotto is so tricky anyway because you have to stand there and stir it constantly. You can't walk away for a second or it sticks to the bottom of the pan. I have this heavy cast iron Dutch oven that I use for everything, though. It's the best. I found it at an estate sale for like twenty bucks. The woman who owned the house must have been a huge collector because she had shelves and shelves of vintage cookware. There were these incredible copper pots, but they were way out of my price range. Copper is supposed to be amazing for heat distribution, but honestly, who has the time to polish it? My mom used to have this brass lamp that she made me polish every spring, and it smelled terrible. Brasso, that's what it was called. Just an awful, chemical smell. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about my mind jumping around? Yeah, I don't really notice that happening. I think I focus just fine when I need to.
Do you have trouble paying attention to details in your work?

Attention to details? I mean, I guess that's actually why I'm here. It's kind of what finally scared me into making this appointment. I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. Like, I'll label the camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note from the director. Or the worst one recently—I exported a whole client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I swore I checked it. 

It's so embarrassing because clients pay a lot of money for these videos. I had this one client, a real estate agent, who wanted this incredibly flashy promo for a luxury condo. The condo was gorgeous, right downtown, huge floor-to-ceiling windows. I love those big windows, but they are a nightmare to shoot around because of the glare. You have to bring in so much extra lighting just to balance the exposure so the room doesn't look like a cave compared to the outside. I used to live in an apartment with tiny windows, and it was so depressing. I ended up buying all these grow lights just so I could keep my houseplants alive. I had this one Monstera plant that got absolutely massive. It practically took over my living room. I had to repot it three times in one year. Repotting is such a messy job, though. I always manage to get potting soil all over the floor, no matter how careful I am. I tried doing it out on my balcony once, but the wind caught the bag of perlite and blew it everywhere. It looked like it had snowed in July. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the mistakes. Yeah, like the wrong lower-thirds or missing timecodes. It's just... it's happening too much lately, and it's really starting to freak me out.
Do you have mood swings?

Mood swings? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I feel like my mood is pretty steady, honestly. I mean, sure, I get annoyed when things go wrong on a shoot, but who wouldn't? 

Like last Tuesday, we were shooting this local commercial, and the main talent was an hour late because he went to the wrong address. He went to our old studio space on 4th Street instead of the new one. 4th Street is an absolute nightmare for parking anyway. I got a ticket there a few months ago because the meter was broken, and when I tried to contest it, the city's website just kept crashing. It looks like it was built in 1995. It has this terrible neon blue background that literally hurts your eyes. Blue is usually my favorite color, too. I actually just painted my bedroom this really deep navy blue. It took three coats of paint because the previous tenant had painted the walls this shocking mustard yellow. I don't know who paints a bedroom yellow, it makes you feel like you're waking up inside a hotdog stand. I do love hotdogs, though, especially the Chicago-style ones with the neon green relish and the celery salt. There's this food truck that parks near my office on Thursdays that makes incredible ones. I always get extra sport peppers on mine. 

Sorry, what did you ask me? Mood swings? Right. No, I don't really get those. I'm pretty even-keeled most of the time.
Do you often struggle to follow through on instructions or finish tasks because you lose focus or get distracted?

Follow through on instructions? Or finish tasks? Um, no, I don't think I really struggle with that. If someone tells me what they need, I get it done. Like if a director says they need a specific transition, I just build it. 

I actually really like building custom transitions. You can do so much with just a little bit of keyframing and some sound design. Sound design is honestly half the magic anyway. You can have the most beautiful footage in the world, but if the audio is garbage, the whole video feels cheap. I was watching this indie film the other night, and the dialogue audio was so muddy I had to turn on the subtitles just to understand what they were saying. I hate using subtitles because I end up just reading the bottom of the screen instead of looking at the cinematography. And the cinematography in this movie was actually really good! They shot it all on vintage anamorphic lenses, which gives you those cool oval bokeh flares. I've been trying to find a good set of vintage lenses on eBay, but the prices have absolutely skyrocketed lately. Everyone wants that retro look now. It's like how suddenly everyone is buying film cameras again. My dad has this old Canon AE-1 sitting in his attic, and I keep meaning to ask him if I can have it. I just need to find a place that still develops 35mm film without charging an arm and a leg. 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about losing focus? No, I don't think so. I finish what I'm supposed to finish.
Do you find it easier to focus on tasks that have a shorter deadline or timeframe?

Shorter deadlines? Um, I'm not really sure if it's easier. I mean, deadlines are just deadlines, right? You just have to hit them. 

Like, we had this really tight turnaround for a social media campaign last month. They needed five different aspect ratios for every single video, which is just so tedious. I don't know why every platform needs a different size now. TikTok wants vertical, YouTube wants horizontal, Instagram wants square, but sometimes they want vertical too. It's impossible to frame a shot that looks good in all of them. You always end up chopping off someone's head or losing half the background. And backgrounds are so important for establishing the vibe. We shot this one interview in a really cool old library, with these massive mahogany bookshelves and those green banker's lamps. I love those lamps. They feel so classic, like something out of a 1940s detective movie. I actually watched The Maltese Falcon recently. Bogart is just so good in it. They don't make movies like that anymore, where the dialogue is just so sharp and fast. It's like watching a tennis match. I tried playing tennis once, but I am terribly uncoordinated. I kept hitting the ball over the fence into the neighbor's yard. They had this huge golden retriever that would just snatch the ball up and refuse to give it back. Dogs are so funny like that. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Deadlines? Yeah, I don't know. I haven't really noticed if short ones are easier. I just do the work.
Do you find it hard to keep your attention on a task for as long as it requires to be completed?

Keep my attention on a task? Um, no, not really. I mean, I sit and edit for hours, so I have to pay attention, right? 

Like, I just upgraded my whole editing bay at home with these dual 4K OLED monitors, and honestly, it makes such a massive difference when you're color grading. I was working on this mini-doc about coral reefs last week, and the blues and greens just pop so much more now. It actually made me really want to go scuba diving again. I went to Cozumel a few years ago with my sister, and the water there is just unbelievably clear. You can see down for like a hundred feet. My sister actually dropped her underwater camera on that trip, just totally let go of the lanyard, and we had to watch it slowly sink all the way to the bottom of the reef. She was so mad because she had all these pictures of this massive sea turtle we saw. Sea turtles are wild, they look like they're flying when they swim. I bought this little carved wooden turtle at a gift shop there, and it's sitting on my desk right now. It's supposed to be a bobblehead, but the spring is broken so it just kind of stares at me with its head tilted while I work. 

Wait, what did you ask? Keeping my attention? Right, no, I don't really have a hard time with that. I just sit down and get the work done.
Do you find that you can focus on a task for a short period but then your attention starts to drift?

Focus for a short period and then drift? Um, I don't really think so. I mean, if I'm working on something, I'm working on it. 

Like yesterday, I was cutting together this sizzle reel for a new reality show, and you just get into the zone, you know? Sizzle reels are actually super fun because you don't have to worry about the narrative making total sense, you just want it to feel high energy. You just slam a bunch of cool shots together with a really heavy bass track. I spent like three hours just looking for the perfect audio track on this licensing site. Those sites are so overwhelming now, they have millions of songs and the search algorithms are terrible. You type in "upbeat acoustic" and it gives you heavy metal. I used to play acoustic guitar back in college. I wasn't very good, but I could play a few Oasis covers. I think everyone who picked up a guitar in the early 2000s learned "Wonderwall." It's practically a requirement. My roommate at the time hated it. She was this classically trained pianist who practiced like six hours a day. She actually ended up moving to Vienna to study at some prestigious conservatory. I always wonder what happened to her. I should try to look her up on Facebook or something, though I hardly ever use Facebook anymore. It's just full of ads and people arguing about politics. 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? My attention drifting? No, I don't think so. I mean, I sit there and do the edits.
Do you find that you can only focus on tasks for a short time before losing interest?

Losing interest quickly? Uh, no, I don't really think that happens to me. I mean, editing is my job, so I have to stay interested enough to finish the project. 

Like right now, I'm working on this promotional video for a local bakery, and it's actually making me so hungry. They make these incredible artisanal sourdough loaves, and the shots of the flour dusting the crust are just gorgeous. I love a good sourdough. I actually tried making my own starter during the pandemic, like everyone else did, right? I named him Clint Yeastwood. But it was so much work! You have to feed it every day and keep it at the exact right temperature. My apartment gets super drafty in the winter because the windows are from like, the 1920s. They have that wavy glass that distorts everything when you look outside. It's really cool aesthetically, but terrible for insulation. I had to buy this heavy-duty plastic film to shrink-wrap over them just to keep my heating bill under a million dollars. I tried using a hairdryer to shrink the plastic, but it actually overheated and tripped the breaker. I had to go down to the scary basement with a flashlight to reset it, and I swear I saw a rat the size of a small cat down there. I've been terrified to go back down ever since. I really need to get my landlord to call an exterminator, but he never answers his phone. 

Um, wait. What were we talking about? Losing interest in things? Yeah, no, I don't think so. I just keep working until it's done.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Distracted by things around me? Um, no, not really. I mean, I work from home, so it's pretty quiet most of the time. 

Unless the neighbor's dog is barking. They have this huge mastiff mix, and he just sits in the yard and barks at the wind. I don't know how they don't hear it. I actually bought these noise-canceling headphones just to block him out, and they are amazing. They're the over-ear kind, and they have this little touch sensor on the side where you just swipe up to turn the volume up. I got them in this really cool matte olive green color. I love olive green, half my wardrobe is that color. I just bought this vintage army jacket from a thrift store last weekend, and it has all these original patches on it. I think it belonged to someone who was stationed in Germany in the 70s. I've always wanted to go to Germany, especially for Oktoberfest. I love soft pretzels. There's this food truck that parks near my gym that sells these massive, warm pretzels with spicy mustard, and it's basically the only reason I go to the gym, so I can justify buying one afterwards. The guy who runs the truck is super nice, he always gives me an extra side of cheese sauce. He said he used to be a chef at a fancy restaurant downtown but got burned out. The restaurant industry is so brutal, I don't know how people do it. 

Oh, sorry, what was the question? Easily distracted? No, I don't think so. I just put my headphones on and focus on my screen.

The restaurant industry is so brutal, I don't know how people do it. 

Oh, sorry, what was the question? Easily distracted? No, I don't think so. I just put my headphones on and focus on my screen.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of inattention, such as making careless mistakes at work and difficulty sustaining focus on tasks, are consistent with a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type (F90.0).
